4f1ebb9b-849a-4202-abbc-3ec11b33af0c.admission_requirements: To be admitted into the BEc(Hons) program, a student must have completed a Bachelor's degree with a major in Economics, Econometrics, Business Economics, Financial Economics, or Business Strategy and Economic Management. A student in a dual degree may gain entry to the BEc(Hons) prior to completing the requirements for the dual degree program if they have completed 144 UOC including all requirements for the relevant major. Students must have completed the equivalent of ECON2101 Microeconomics 2 and ECON2102 Macroeconomics 2, plus an econometrics course requirement that depends on the specialisation. It is also recommended that a student complete ECON3202 Mathematical Economics, or an equivalent, before commencing the BEc(Hons). A student must have an overall Weighted Average Mark (WAM) of at least 70 (or equivalent) with a discipline/major WAM of at least 70; the WAM required for entry may be higher depending on discipline and place availability. Full-time and part-time (over 3 semesters) study is available.

927c988d-37b3-4db1-84d9-8d73ed537771.description: UNSW's Bachelor of Engineering Science (BEngSc, program 3706) is a 3-year, non-accredited pass degree that functions as the university's internal exit award for the Bachelor of Engineering (Honours). Students are transferred into it, with faculty consent, when they do not meet the academic-standing requirements to continue in a BE(Hons) discipline stream, rather than choosing it as a direct first-preference qualification; a small number of students who show sustained improvement can apply to transfer back into the BE(Hons) program. It retains the same engineering major (drawn from the student's original BE(Hons) discipline stream) plus free electives and general education, giving a genuine engineering qualification and credit pathway for students who do not complete the Honours degree, rather than leaving with no engineering credential at all.
927c988d-37b3-4db1-84d9-8d73ed537771.admission_requirements: The Bachelor of Engineering Science is not a direct UAC/first-preference entry program. Students are admitted by internal transfer from the Bachelor of Engineering (Honours) when they do not meet BE(Hons) academic-standing/progression requirements, per UNSW Engineering Faculty policy (Bachelor of Engineering Science program information page). Readmission to the BE(Hons) is possible on application, subject to a minimum of 48 UOC completed in the BEngSc program, meeting the BE(Hons) progression WAM, having passed any previously failed core courses, being in good academic standing, and being able to complete the BE(Hons) within the maximum time to complete.

e05a9f98-c4fc-47f4-af26-637a04273d2c.admission_requirements: For the 2.5-year, 108 UOC program: a bachelor degree with a credit average in a related field (built environment disciplines, engineering, business or law), OR a bachelor degree in any field with a credit average plus three years of construction-industry experience at a managerial level, OR a Graduate Certificate in Construction Project Management or Graduate Certificate in Property and Development with a credit average. For the accelerated 2-year, 84 UOC program: an undergraduate honours degree with a credit average in a related field, OR an undergraduate honours degree in an unrelated field plus three years of construction-industry experience at a managerial level, OR a master's degree with a credit average in a related field. Applicants who don't meet these criteria may enter via the Graduate Certificate in Construction Project Management or Graduate Certificate in Property and Development as a pathway.

8258db93-4fb6-4d04-a1c7-c53630a6ff6b.admission_requirements: Inherited from the base Master of Public Health (Extension) admission pathway (program 9046), which this combined program shares. There are two standard pathways, plus a third exceptional pathway: (1) a three-year undergraduate degree in any field plus two years of full-time professional or volunteer experience in a relevant field (health, allied health, medicine, nursing, social work, psychology, paramedicine, environmental health, health administration, policy studies, development studies, or health-focused roles in emergency services, management, research, engineering, law, science, economics, journalism or policy), OR (2) an undergraduate degree plus honours, or a postgraduate degree, in a relevant field, OR (3) in exceptional circumstances, extensive professional health experience (minimum five years full-time) without a relevant degree, assessed via interview with the School of Population Health. Domestic applicants apply via UAC; international applicants apply via UNSW Apply Online.

27b6f5b2-27f8-4a03-b83c-d861dbaefe36._fabrication_fix: Original curriculum invented a 'COMPAT Software Engineering' specialisation that does not exist in the real handbook (program 8543), and omitted the real default specialisation COMPMS. Rebuilt from the live handbook overview.
27b6f5b2-27f8-4a03-b83c-d861dbaefe36.curriculum: Foundation Courses (for students without a computing background): COMP9020 Foundations of Computer Science, COMP9021 Principles of Programming, COMP9024 Data Structures and Algorithms, COMP9820 Software Project Management, COMP9920 Ethics of Computer Science and Engineering. Students must complete one specialisation: COMPMS Information Technology (the default specialisation if none is nominated), COMPLS Artificial Intelligence, COMPNS Database Systems, COMPOS Internetworking, or COMPXS Cyber Security Engineering. A second specialisation can be added from the approved combinations: COMPLS with COMPNS, COMPLS with COMPOS, COMPXS with COMPNS, COMPXS with COMPOS, or COMPNS with COMPOS. Advanced standing of up to one year is available for students with an appropriate prior qualification.
